title: SpaceX's $60 Billion Cursor Acquisition Shakes Up the AI Coding Wars
excerpt: The all-stock deal gives Elon Musk's rocket-turned-AI empire a direct line into the enterprise coding tools market dominated by OpenAI and Anthropic.
body:
• SpaceX exercised its option to acquire AI coding startup Cursor (Anysphere) for $60 billion in an all-stock deal
  • The acquisition bolsters xAI's position in the enterprise AI tools market, giving it access to millions of developers' coding data
  • Cursor reached $100 million in annual recurring revenue within two years, fueled by the rise of "vibe coding"
  • The deal, expected to close in Q3 2026, follows SpaceX's record-breaking Nasdaq IPO that valued the company at over $2 trillion

Musk Bets Big on AI Coding

SpaceX has exercised its option to acquire Cursor, the AI coding startup behind one of the fastest-growing developer tools in Silicon Valley, for $60 billion in an all-stock transaction, according to a regulatory filing. The deal marks Elon Musk's most aggressive move yet to challenge OpenAI and Anthropic in the lucrative enterprise AI market.

https://x.com/prateek_madaan1/status/2088531127887606121

The acquisition brings Cursor — formally known as Anysphere — under the umbrella of xAI, SpaceX's AI division that was merged into the company in February. Cursor investors will receive SpaceX stock based on the startup's $60 billion equity value, with the transaction expected to close in the third quarter of 2026.

From Rockets to Code Editors

Founded in 2022 by MIT graduates Michael Truell, Sualeh Asif, Aman Sanger and Arvid Lunnemark, Cursor has grown rapidly by capitalizing on the trend of "vibe coding" — using natural-language prompts to generate and edit software. The startup hit approximately $100 million in annual recurring revenue within two years and had previously raised around $3.4 billion from investors including Thrive Capital, Andreessen Horowitz and Accel at a $29 billion valuation.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=8bX4ljT044Y

SpaceX had been eyeing Cursor for months. In April, the company secured an option to either buy the startup for $60 billion or pay $10 billion for a partnership. The full acquisition was delayed until after SpaceX's blockbuster Nasdaq debut, which saw its valuation surge past $2 trillion.

"Cursor does not have the scale of OpenAI or Anthropic, but it has built some very impressive coding models relative to cost. That makes this a positive move for SpaceX."

— Matt Britzman, senior equity analyst, Hargreaves Lansdown

Building a Vertically Integrated AI Stack

Industry analysts see the deal as a strategic move to create a vertically integrated AI development stack. With xAI's Colossus supercomputing infrastructure underneath, its foundation models in the middle, and Cursor's coding product on top, SpaceX is assembling a full supply chain for AI-powered software development.

"Elon Musk is attempting to warp space and time to leap ahead in the AI race," said Mitch Ashley, vice president at The Futurum Group. "This is the strategic template AI coding is collapsing toward, matching patterns already visible with OpenAI/Microsoft, Google, and Anthropic/AWS."

Cursor had acknowledged that limited access to computing power had "bottlenecked" its growth. Under SpaceX, the startup will gain access to xAI's infrastructure, including the Colossus supercomputer used for training AI models.

What It Means for Developers

SpaceX said it would release an AI model on Cursor as well as Grok Build, xAI's coding agent, which has been jointly trained with Cursor's team for several months. The move puts SpaceX in direct competition for the developer workflow — a market that has become one of the first areas where companies have turned AI into a real source of revenue.

In its IPO filing, SpaceX estimated a $28.5 trillion total addressable market, with roughly 93 percent connected to AI. The company noted that Cursor's access to developers' data — including coding requests and design decisions — could help improve its AI models, including Grok.

What's Next

The transaction is on track to close in the coming weeks. For the broader AI industry, the deal signals a new phase of consolidation, where access to computing power and developer ecosystems may matter more than model quality alone. Anthropic and OpenAI, both backed by deep-pocketed cloud partners, now face a rival with its own infrastructure, a public market war chest, and a direct pipeline to millions of developers worldwide.
